weeks.note: A northern town, a radio show and a tea house. Listen for でも, じゃあ and なるほど doing their jobs.

paragraphs.ja: {今日|きょう}、{北|きた}の{小|ちい}さい{町|まち}に{来|き}ました。{海|うみ}の{近|ちか}くの{町|まち}です。
paragraphs.en: Today I came to a small town in the north. It's a town near the sea.

paragraphs.ja: {空|そら}は{白|しろ}いです。{風|かぜ}が{強|つよ}いです。{冬|ふゆ}はもうすぐです。
paragraphs.en: The sky is white. The wind is strong. Winter is almost here.

paragraphs.ja: {町|まち}の{人|ひと}は{少|すく}ないです。でも、{船|ふね}は{多|おお}いです。{朝|あさ}、{船|ふね}が{港|みなと}を{出|で}ます。
paragraphs.en: There aren't many people in the town. But there are a lot of boats. In the morning, the boats leave the harbor.

paragraphs.ja: {夜|よる}、{外|そと}に{出|で}ました。{月|つき}がとても{明|あか}るかったです。{星|ほし}もたくさん{見|み}えました。
paragraphs.en: At night I went outside. The moon was very bright. I could see lots of stars too.

paragraphs.ja: {家|いえ}で、{魚|さかな}とご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べました。お{茶|ちゃ}も{飲|の}みました。
paragraphs.en: At home I ate fish and rice. I had some tea too.

paragraphs.ja: {明日|あした}は{一日|いちにち}、{町|まち}の{音|おと}を{聞|き}きます。{風|かぜ}の{音|おと}、{船|ふね}の{音|おと}、{鳥|とり}の{声|こえ}。やっぱり、{新|あたら}しい{場所|ばしょ}はいいですね。
paragraphs.en: Tomorrow I'll spend the whole day listening to the town's sounds. The wind, the boats, the birds. A new place really is good.

questions.prompt: この{町|まち}はどこにありますか。
questions.en: Where is this town?

options.why: 「{海|うみ}の{近|ちか}くの{町|まち}です」: it's a town near the sea.
No mountain in this one. The town is by the sea, with boats and a harbor.

options.text: {大|おお}きい{町|まち}の{中|なか}
options.why: It's a small town (「{小|ちい}さい{町|まち}」), and not inside a bigger one.

questions.prompt: この{町|まち}に{多|おお}いのは{何|なん}ですか。
questions.en: What is there a lot of in this town?

options.why: 「でも、{船|ふね}は{多|おお}いです」
The opposite: 「{町|まち}の{人|ひと}は{少|すく}ないです」.
Shops aren't mentioned.

questions.prompt: {夜|よる}、{何|なに}が{見|み}えましたか。
questions.en: What could the writer see at night?

options.why: The moon was bright, and 「{星|ほし}もたくさん{見|み}えました」.
Winter is almost here, but no snow has fallen yet.
The boats leave in the morning. At night it was the sky.

questions.prompt: 「でも、{船|ふね}は{多|おお}いです」の「でも」は、{何|なに}をしていますか。
questions.en: What is でも doing in 「でも、船は多いです」?

options.text: Turning: few people, but lots of boats
options.why: でも sets the second fact against the first. Notice the は on both: 人は… 船は… is the contrast.
That would be それに. Here the two facts pull in opposite directions.
That would be だから. Few people isn't the reason there are many boats.

readings.title: {夜|よる}の{音楽|おんがく}{番組|ばんぐみ}

paragraphs.ja: こんばんは。{夜|よる}の{音楽|おんがく}{番組|ばんぐみ}です。{今日|きょう}も{新|あたら}しい{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}きましょう。
paragraphs.en: Good evening. This is the night music program. Let's listen to some new music again today.

paragraphs.ja: {今日|きょう}のゲストは{作曲家|さっきょくか}です。{電話|でんわ}で{話|はな}します。もしもし？
paragraphs.en: Today's guest is a composer. We're talking on the phone. Hello?

paragraphs.ja: ゲスト：「もしもし、こんばんは。{今|いま}、{外|そと}は{北風|きたかぜ}が{強|つよ}いです。」
paragraphs.en: Guest: "Hello, good evening. The north wind is strong outside right now."

paragraphs.ja: 「へえ、そうなんですか。じゃあ、{答|こた}えてください。{一番|いちばん}{楽|たの}しい{音|おと}は{何|なん}ですか。」
paragraphs.en: "Oh, really? Then tell me: what's the most fun sound?"

paragraphs.ja: 「えっと…{雲|くも}の{下|した}の{海|うみ}の{音|おと}です。それから、{電車|でんしゃ}の{音|おと}も{好|す}きです。」
paragraphs.en: "Um… the sound of the sea under the clouds. And I like the sound of trains too."

paragraphs.ja: 「なるほど。{今日|きょう}の{会話|かいわ}、{楽|たの}しかったです。では、{音楽|おんがく}をどうぞ。」
paragraphs.en: "I see. I enjoyed our conversation today. And now, here's the music."

questions.prompt: これは{何|なん}の{番組|ばんぐみ}ですか。
questions.en: What kind of program is this?

options.text: {音楽|おんがく}の{番組|ばんぐみ}
options.why: 「{夜|よる}の{音楽|おんがく}{番組|ばんぐみ}です」

options.text: ニュースの{番組|ばんぐみ}
options.why: No news. It's music and a guest.

options.text: {料理|りょうり}の{番組|ばんぐみ}
options.why: Nobody cooks. The talk is about sounds.

questions.prompt: ゲストとは、{何|なに}で{話|はな}しますか。
questions.en: How does the host talk with the guest?

options.why: 「{電話|でんわ}で{話|はな}します」: で marks the means (Lesson 2). That's why the guest says もしもし.
The guest is outside, in the wind, not in the studio.
No letters. They're talking live.

questions.prompt: ゲストが{好|す}きな{音|おと}は？
questions.en: Which sounds does the guest like?

options.text: {海|うみ}と{電車|でんしゃ}の{音|おと}
options.why: The sea under the clouds, 「それから、{電車|でんしゃ}の{音|おと}も」.
The guest only says the wind is strong. Not that they like it.
Birds aren't mentioned.

questions.prompt: {最後|さいご}の「なるほど」は、{何|なに}をしていますか。
questions.en: What is the final なるほど doing?

options.text: Showing the answer made sense to the host
options.why: なるほど = "I see, that makes sense." It closes the answer before moving on.
なるほど accepts what was said. Disagreeing would sound more like うーん or でも….
It wraps up. The very next thing is the music.

paragraphs.ja: {平日|へいじつ}の{午後|ごご}、{古|ふる}い{茶屋|ちゃや}に{入|はい}りました。{中|なか}は{和室|わしつ}です。{客|きゃく}は{私|わたし}{一人|ひとり}でした。
paragraphs.en: On a weekday afternoon I went into an old tea house. Inside it's a Japanese-style room. I was the only customer.

paragraphs.ja: {店|みせ}の{人|ひと}：「いらっしゃいませ。」{私|わたし}：「すみません、この{辺|へん}の{名物|めいぶつ}は{何|なん}ですか。」
paragraphs.en: Shopkeeper: "Welcome." Me: "Excuse me, what's the local specialty around here?"

paragraphs.ja: 「うちは{魚|さかな}の{定食|ていしょく}が{名物|めいぶつ}です。{近|ちか}くの{魚屋|さかなや}の{魚|さかな}ですよ。」
paragraphs.en: "Our fish set meal is what we're known for. The fish comes from the fish shop nearby."

paragraphs.ja: 「じゃあ、それをお{願|ねが}いします。」{間|ま}もなく、{食事|しょくじ}が{来|き}ました。
paragraphs.en: "Then I'll have that, please." Soon the meal arrived.

paragraphs.ja: {外|そと}に{小|ちい}さい{鳥|とり}がいました。{店|みせ}の{人|ひと}は「あの{鳥|とり}は{毎年|まいとし}{来|き}ますよ」と{言|い}いました。「へえ、そうなんですね。」
paragraphs.en: There was a small bird outside. The shopkeeper said, "That bird comes every year." "Oh, really."

paragraphs.ja: {食事|しょくじ}の{後|あと}、{東|ひがし}の{歩道|ほどう}を{少|すこ}し{歩|ある}きました。{来年|らいねん}も{必|かなら}ずこの{場所|ばしょ}に{来|き}ます。
paragraphs.en: After the meal I walked a little along the sidewalk to the east. I'll definitely come back to this place next year.

questions.prompt: {茶屋|ちゃや}の{中|なか}は、どんな{部屋|へや}でしたか。
questions.en: What kind of room was the inside of the tea house?

options.why: 「{中|なか}は{和室|わしつ}です」: a Japanese-style room.

options.text: {客|きゃく}が{多|おお}い{部屋|へや}
options.why: The writer was the only customer (「{私|わたし}{一人|ひとり}」).
It's an old tea house (「{古|ふる}い{茶屋|ちゃや}」).

questions.prompt: この{店|みせ}の{名物|めいぶつ}は{何|なん}ですか。
questions.en: What is this shop known for?

options.text: {魚|さかな}の{定食|ていしょく}
options.why: 「{魚|さかな}の{定食|ていしょく}が{名物|めいぶつ}です」: が picks out which dish (Lesson 1).
It's a tea house, but the dish they name is the fish set meal.
The bird is a visitor outside, not on the menu.

questions.prompt: 「{間|ま}もなく、{食事|しょくじ}が{来|き}ました」。{食事|しょくじ}はいつ{来|き}ましたか。
questions.en: When did the meal arrive?

options.why: 間もなく = soon, shortly. The meal came quickly.
間もなく means it didn't take long.
Next year is when the writer will come back.

questions.prompt: あの{鳥|とり}は、いつ{来|き}ますか。
questions.en: When does that bird come?

options.why: 「あの{鳥|とり}は{毎年|まいとし}{来|き}ますよ」
Every year, not every day.
Weekday is when the writer visited. The bird comes every year.

weeks.note: Verb pairs in the wild: 見える, 出る and 見せる turn up in all three.

paragraphs.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}に、{友人|ゆうじん}と{山|やま}に{上|のぼ}りました。{大|おお}きい{山|やま}ではありません。{小|ちい}さい{山|やま}です。
paragraphs.en: On my day off I climbed a mountain with a friend. Not a big mountain. A small one.

paragraphs.ja: {朝|あさ}、{村|むら}を{出|で}ました。{川|かわ}の{右|みぎ}の{道|みち}を{歩|ある}きました。{空|そら}は{青|あお}かったです。
paragraphs.en: In the morning we left the village. We walked the path on the right side of the river. The sky was blue.

paragraphs.ja: {上|うえ}まで{一時間|いちじかん}でした。{上|うえ}から、{下|した}の{村|むら}と{田|た}んぼが{見|み}えました。
paragraphs.en: It was an hour to the top. From up there we could see the village and the rice fields below.

paragraphs.ja: {友人|ゆうじん}は「わあ、すごい！」と{言|い}いました。{私|わたし}は{写真|しゃしん}を{少|すこ}し{撮|と}りました。
paragraphs.en: My friend said, "Wow, amazing!" I took a few photos.

paragraphs.ja: {二人|ふたり}で、{丸|まる}いおにぎりを{食|た}べました。{水|みず}も{少|すこ}しありました。
paragraphs.en: The two of us ate round rice balls. We had a little water too.

paragraphs.ja: {下|した}までは{早|はや}かったです。でも、{今|いま}、{足|あし}が{少|すこ}し{痛|いた}いです。まあ、やっぱり{山|やま}はいいですね。
paragraphs.en: The way down was fast. But now my legs hurt a little. Well, mountains really are the best.

questions.prompt: だれと{山|やま}に{上|のぼ}りましたか。
questions.en: Who did the writer climb the mountain with?

options.why: 「{友人|ゆうじん}と{山|やま}に{上|のぼ}りました」: と marks who you do it with.
「{二人|ふたり}で」 comes later: there were two of them.
The village is where they started, not who came along.

questions.prompt: {上|うえ}から、{何|なに}が{見|み}えましたか。
questions.en: What could they see from the top?

options.why: 「{下|した}の{村|むら}と{田|た}んぼが{見|み}えました」: が + 見える, the view came into sight.
No sea in this one. It's a village and rice fields below.
The writer says this one isn't a big mountain, and nothing says another one was visible.

questions.prompt: {今|いま}、どこが{痛|いた}いですか。
questions.en: What hurts now?

options.why: 「{足|あし}が{少|すこ}し{痛|いた}いです」
Hands aren't mentioned. It's the legs, after the walk down.
Eyes aren't mentioned. It's the legs.

questions.prompt: 「まあ、やっぱり{山|やま}はいいですね」の「まあ」は、{何|なに}をしていますか。
questions.en: What is まあ doing in 「まあ、やっぱり山はいいですね」?

options.text: Shrugging off the sore legs: "well, anyway"
options.why: まあ softens and moves on: the legs hurt, but never mind. Then やっぱり confirms what they already felt about mountains.
Surprise is the friend's わあ at the top. まあ is calmer: "well…"
Nothing is being asked. ですね shares a feeling.

paragraphs.ja: 「もしもし、ケンさん？{今|いま}、{駅|えき}を{出|で}ました。でも、{道|みち}が{分|わ}かりません。」
paragraphs.en: "Hello, Ken? I just left the station. But I don't know the way."

paragraphs.ja: 「えっと、{近|ちか}くに{何|なに}がありますか。」「{大|おお}きい{通|とお}りと、{交番|こうばん}があります。」
paragraphs.en: "Um, what's near you?" "There's a big avenue and a police box."

paragraphs.ja: 「ああ、{分|わ}かりました。{交番|こうばん}の{人|ひと}に、{住所|じゅうしょ}を{見|み}せてください。」
paragraphs.en: "Ah, got it. Show the address to the officer at the police box."

paragraphs.ja: {交番|こうばん}の{人|ひと}は{親切|しんせつ}でした。「{一番|いちばん}{近|ちか}い{道|みち}は、この{通|とお}りです。{海|うみ}の{方|ほう}に{行|い}ってください。」
paragraphs.en: The officer was kind. "The shortest way is this avenue. Go toward the sea."

paragraphs.ja: {会話|かいわ}は{全部|ぜんぶ}{日本語|にほんご}でした！{少|すこ}し{歩|ある}きました。ケンさんの{家|いえ}は、{海|うみ}の{近|ちか}くにありました。
paragraphs.en: The whole conversation was in Japanese! I walked a little. Ken's house was near the sea.

paragraphs.ja: 「よかった！{電話|でんわ}、ありがとう。」「いえいえ。じゃあ、おやつを{食|た}べましょう。」
paragraphs.en: "Phew! Thanks for the call." "No problem. Right, let's have a snack."

questions.prompt: {駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くに{何|なに}がありましたか。
questions.en: What was near the station?

options.text: {大|おお}きい{通|とお}りと{交番|こうばん}
options.why: 「{大|おお}きい{通|とお}りと、{交番|こうばん}があります」
The sea is where the officer says to head, and where Ken's house is, not what was by the station.
If the house were by the station, there'd be no phone call.

questions.prompt: {交番|こうばん}の{人|ひと}に{何|なに}を{見|み}せましたか。
questions.en: What did the writer show the officer?

options.why: 「{住所|じゅうしょ}を{見|み}せてください」: 見せる = make someone see it, show.
The phone is how they talked to Ken. What Ken said to show was the address.
A name doesn't help you find a house. It was the address.

questions.prompt: {会話|かいわ}は{何語|なにご}でしたか。
questions.en: What language was the conversation in?

options.text: {全部|ぜんぶ}{日本語|にほんご}
options.why: 「{会話|かいわ}は{全部|ぜんぶ}{日本語|にほんご}でした！」, and the ！ says the writer is proud of it.
全部 = all of it.
The point of the exclamation is that it was all Japanese.

questions.prompt: 「じゃあ、おやつを{食|た}べましょう」の「じゃあ」は、{何|なに}をしていますか。
questions.en: What is じゃあ doing here?

options.text: Moving on now that the problem is solved: "right, so…"
options.why: じゃあ closes one topic and moves to the next. The guest has arrived, so: snack time.
There's nothing to disagree with. That would be でも.
Surprise would be えっ or へえ. じゃあ is a hinge to the next thing.

readings.title: お{部屋|へや}のご{案内|あんない}

paragraphs.ja: ようこそ。お{部屋|へや}は「{竹|たけ}」の{和室|わしつ}です。お{部屋|へや}から{西|にし}の{海|うみ}が{見|み}えます。
paragraphs.en: Welcome. Your room is the Bamboo room, a Japanese-style room. You can see the sea to the west from it.

paragraphs.ja: お{食事|しょくじ}は{下|した}の{部屋|へや}です。{朝|あさ}ごはんは{七時|しちじ}から、{晩|ばん}ごはんは{六時|ろくじ}からです。{和食|わしょく}です。
paragraphs.en: Meals are in the room downstairs. Breakfast is from seven, dinner from six. Japanese food.

paragraphs.ja: {近|ちか}くに{魚屋|さかなや}と{本屋|ほんや}があります。{魚屋|さかなや}の{魚|さかな}は、{本当|ほんとう}においしいですよ。
paragraphs.en: There's a fish shop and a bookshop nearby. The fish at the fish shop is really good.

paragraphs.ja: {夜|よる}は、{後|うし}ろの{山|やま}の{辺|あた}りで、{星|ほし}がよく{見|み}えます。{光|ひか}る{星|ほし}がたくさんあります。
paragraphs.en: At night, around the hill behind us, you can see the stars well. There are lots of shining stars.

paragraphs.ja: {床|ゆか}はちょっと{古|ふる}いです。{歩|ある}くと、{音|おと}がします。すみません！
paragraphs.en: The floor is a bit old. It creaks when you walk. Sorry!

paragraphs.ja: {何|なん}でも、{家|いえ}の{者|もの}に{言|い}ってください。どうぞ、ゆっくり{休|やす}んでくださいね。
paragraphs.en: Tell any of us if you need anything. Please, rest and take your time.

questions.prompt: お{部屋|へや}から{何|なに}が{見|み}えますか。
questions.en: What can you see from the room?

options.why: 「お{部屋|へや}から{西|にし}の{海|うみ}が{見|み}えます」
The hill is behind the inn, and it's where to see stars at night. The view from the room is the sea, to the west.
The fish shop is nearby, but the note doesn't say you can see it from the room.

questions.prompt: {晩|ばん}ごはんは{何時|なんじ}からですか。
questions.en: What time does dinner start?

options.why: 「{晩|ばん}ごはんは{六時|ろくじ}からです」
Seven is breakfast.
Eight isn't in the note.

questions.prompt: {星|ほし}はどこでよく{見|み}えますか。
questions.en: Where can you see the stars well?

options.text: {後|うし}ろの{山|やま}の{辺|あた}り
options.why: 「{後|うし}ろの{山|やま}の{辺|あた}りで、{星|ほし}がよく{見|み}えます」
The room downstairs is for meals.
The sea is the view from the room. Stars are over the hill behind.

questions.prompt: {床|ゆか}を{歩|ある}くと、どうなりますか。
questions.en: What happens when you walk on the floor?

options.why: 「{歩|ある}くと、{音|おと}がします」: 音がする = a sound is heard. The old floor creaks; nobody is making the noise on purpose.
音を出す = someone makes a sound deliberately, like playing a drum. The creaking floor isn't anyone's plan.
光る is for the stars in the paragraph before. The floor just creaks.

weeks.note: Week 2: a snowy morning built from newly burned words, a valley town from enlightened ones, and a note from a friend for master and guru.

paragraphs.ja: {朝|あさ}、{外|そと}は{白|しろ}かったです。{雪|ゆき}です！{今年|ことし}はじめての{雪|ゆき}です。
paragraphs.en: In the morning it was white outside. Snow! The first snow of the year.

paragraphs.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{近|ちか}くの{店|みせ}でコーヒーを{買|か}います。でも、{今日|きょう}は{雪|ゆき}が{多|おお}いです。{家|いえ}でお{茶|ちゃ}を{入|い}れました。
paragraphs.en: Every morning I buy coffee at a shop nearby. But today there's a lot of snow. I made tea at home.

paragraphs.ja: {朝|あさ}ごはんの{後|あと}、{弟|おとうと}に{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}きました。{弟|おとうと}は{雪|ゆき}が{大好|だいす}きです。
paragraphs.en: After breakfast I wrote a letter to my younger brother. He loves snow.

paragraphs.ja: {午後|ごご}、{雪|ゆき}が{止|や}みました。{外|そと}に{出|で}て、{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}りました。{空|そら}が{本当|ほんとう}に{青|あお}かったです。
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon the snow stopped. I went out and took photos. The sky was really blue.

paragraphs.ja: {夜|よる}、{友人|ゆうじん}から{電話|でんわ}がありました。「{雪|ゆき}、すごいね！」「うん、やっぱり{冬|ふゆ}はいいね。」
paragraphs.en: At night a friend called. "The snow — amazing, right?" "Yeah, winter really is the best."

paragraphs.ja: {明日|あした}も{雪|ゆき}かな。じゃあ、{明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}も{家|いえ}でお{茶|ちゃ}です。
paragraphs.en: Snow tomorrow too, I wonder. Then tomorrow morning it's tea at home again.

questions.prompt: {毎朝|まいあさ}、どこでコーヒーを{買|か}いますか。
questions.en: Where does the writer buy coffee every morning?

options.why: 「{毎朝|まいあさ}、{近|ちか}くの{店|みせ}でコーヒーを{買|か}います」
Home is where the tea got made today, because of the snow. Coffee usually comes from the shop.
No station in this one. It's a shop nearby.

questions.prompt: {弟|おとうと}は{何|なに}が{大好|だいす}きですか。
questions.en: What does the younger brother love?

options.why: 「{弟|おとうと}は{雪|ゆき}が{大好|だいす}きです」: は is the brother (topic), が picks out what he loves.
The tea is the writer's, not the brother's.
The letter is what the writer sent him. Nothing says he loves letters.

questions.prompt: {午後|ごご}、{空|そら}はどうでしたか。
questions.en: How was the sky in the afternoon?

options.why: 「{空|そら}が{本当|ほんとう}に{青|あお}かったです」: once the snow stopped, the sky cleared.

questions.prompt: 「やっぱり{冬|ふゆ}はいいね」の「やっぱり」は、{何|なに}をしていますか。

options.text: Confirming a feeling the friend already had
options.why: やっぱり = "just as I thought, after all." The snow confirms what they already believed about winter.
That's でも or だけど. やっぱり agrees with something, it doesn't turn against it.
That's ちょっと or 少し.

paragraphs.ja: {今日|きょう}は{谷|たに}の{小|ちい}さい{町|まち}に{来|き}ました。{天気|てんき}はいいです。{空|そら}が{明|あか}るいです。
paragraphs.en: Today I came to a small town in a valley. The weather's good. The sky is bright.

paragraphs.ja: {地図|ちず}を{見|み}ましたが、{道|みち}が{分|わ}かりません。{角|かど}に{交番|こうばん}がありました。
paragraphs.en: I looked at the map, but I couldn't work out the way. There was a police box on the corner.

paragraphs.ja: 「すみません、この{辺|へん}に{古|ふる}い{石|いし}の{橋|はし}がありますか。」「ありますよ。{池|いけ}の{近|ちか}くです。{歩|ある}いて{五分|ごふん}ぐらいです。」

paragraphs.en: "Is it a famous spot?" "Yes, the most famous one in town. But at this time of day there are a lot of people."

paragraphs.ja: {橋|はし}の{下|した}に{川|かわ}がありました。{川|かわ}の{音|おと}は{音楽|おんがく}みたいでした。

paragraphs.ja: {明日|あした}は{朝|あさ}{早|はや}く、{森|もり}の{道|みち}を{歩|ある}きます。{天気|てんき}は{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}かな。
paragraphs.en: Tomorrow, early in the morning, I'll walk the forest path. I hope the weather holds.

questions.prompt: {交番|こうばん}はどこにありましたか。
questions.en: Where was the police box?

options.why: 「{角|かど}に{交番|こうばん}がありました」: に because it just exists there.
Near the pond is where the bridge is.
Under the bridge is the river.

questions.prompt: {橋|はし}まで、{歩|ある}いて{何分|なんぷん}ぐらいですか。
questions.en: About how many minutes to the bridge on foot?

options.why: 「{歩|ある}いて{五分|ごふん}ぐらいです」
Much less: it's close, near the pond.
The writer didn't know the way at first, but the officer gives the time: five minutes.

questions.prompt: {今|いま}の{時間|じかん}、{橋|はし}はどうですか。
questions.en: What's the bridge like at this time of day?

options.why: 「{今|いま}の{時間|じかん}は{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いですよ」: でも flags it as the catch.
少ない is the opposite of what the officer says.
The weather is good; the sky is bright.

questions.prompt: 「{音楽|おんがく}みたいでした」の「みたい」は、{何|なに}をしていますか。
questions.en: What is みたい doing in 「音楽みたいでした」?

options.why: Noun + みたい = "like ~, resembling ~." The river isn't music; it reminds the writer of it.
That's 〜たい (聞きたい). みたい after a noun compares.
That's 〜てみる. Similar sound, different job.

paragraphs.ja: {先日|せんじつ}はありがとう！{和食|わしょく}の{食事|しょくじ}、{楽|たの}しかったですね。
paragraphs.en: Thanks for the other day! That Japanese dinner was fun, wasn't it.

paragraphs.ja: {私|わたし}は{夕方|ゆうがた}まで{出|で}かけます。{部屋|へや}の{鍵|かぎ}はテーブルの{上|うえ}です。
paragraphs.en: I'm out until evening. The room key is on the table.

paragraphs.ja: {近|ちか}くに{魚屋|さかなや}と{茶屋|ちゃや}があります。{茶屋|ちゃや}のお{茶|ちゃ}は{本当|ほんとう}においしいですよ。
paragraphs.en: There's a fish shop and a tea house nearby. The tea at the tea house is really good.

paragraphs.ja: {夜|よる}は{星|ほし}がよく{見|み}えます。{和室|わしつ}の{後|うし}ろの{窓|まど}から、{海|うみ}も{見|み}えますよ。
paragraphs.en: At night you can see the stars well. From the window at the back of the tatami room, you can see the sea, too.

paragraphs.ja: {明日|あした}の{夜明|よあ}けに、{鳥|とり}の{声|こえ}を{録音|ろくおん}しませんか。いい{場所|ばしょ}があります。
paragraphs.en: Want to record the birds at dawn tomorrow? There's a good spot.

paragraphs.ja: {後|あと}で{私|わたし}の{絵|え}を{見|み}せますね。じゃあ、また{夕方|ゆうがた}に！
paragraphs.en: I'll show you my paintings later. OK, see you this evening!

questions.prompt: {友|とも}だちは{夕方|ゆうがた}まで{何|なに}をしますか。
questions.en: What is the friend doing until evening?

options.why: 「{夕方|ゆうがた}まで{出|で}かけます」: out of the house until evening.
The friend is out; only the key is in the room.

options.text: {鳥|とり}の{声|こえ}を{録音|ろくおん}します
options.why: That's the plan for tomorrow at dawn, not today.

questions.prompt: {和室|わしつ}の{後|うし}ろの{窓|まど}から、{何|なに}が{見|み}えますか。
questions.en: What can you see from the window at the back of the tatami room?

options.why: 「{後|うし}ろの{窓|まど}から、{海|うみ}も{見|み}えますよ」
The fish shop is nearby, but the note doesn't say you can see it.
The tea house is nearby too; the window shows the sea.

questions.prompt: 「{夜明|よあ}け」はいつですか。
questions.en: When is 夜明け?

options.text: {朝|あさ}、とても{早|はや}い{時間|じかん}
options.why: 夜明け is when the night (夜) opens up (明ける): dawn, the very start of the morning.
夕方 is evening, when the friend comes back.
夜 is part of the word, but 夜明け is the moment the night ends, not the night itself.

questions.prompt: {後|あと}で、{友|とも}だちは{何|なに}を{見|み}せますか。
questions.en: What will the friend show later?

options.why: 「{後|あと}で{私|わたし}の{絵|え}を{見|み}せますね」: 見せる = to show.
You can see the stars yourself at night (見えます); the friend isn't showing them.
The key is already on the table.

weeks.note: First batch: a rainy day off, a station in Kyushu, and a menu full of burned numbers.

paragraphs.ja: {今日|きょう}は{休日|きゅうじつ}です。でも、{朝|あさ}から{雨|あめ}です。{空|そら}は{白|しろ}いです。

paragraphs.en: After breakfast I made coffee. The dog is resting under the bed.

questions.prompt: {朝|あさ}の{天気|てんき}はどうでしたか。
questions.en: What was the weather like in the morning?

options.why: 「{朝|あさ}から{雨|あめ}です」: it's been raining since the morning.

options.text: いい{天気|てんき}でした
options.why: The first paragraph says {朝|あさ}から{雨|あめ}です, so it wasn't nice out.

options.text: {空|そら}が{青|あお}かったです
options.why: 「{空|そら}は{白|しろ}いです」: the sky was white (overcast), not blue.

questions.prompt: {犬|いぬ}はどこで{休|やす}んでいましたか。
questions.en: Where was the dog resting?

options.why: 「ベッドの{下|した}で{休|やす}んでいます」: under the bed.
テーブルの{上|うえ} is "on the table." The passage says ベッドの{下|した}, under the bed.
The dog goes to the shop later, in the afternoon. In the morning it was at home under the bed.

questions.prompt: {店|みせ}の{人|ひと}は{何|なん}と{言|い}いましたか。
questions.en: What did the shopkeeper say?

options.why: 「{今日|きょう}は{人|ひと}が{少|すく}ないですね」: not many people today.
{多|おお}い is the opposite of {少|すく}ない. The rain kept people home.
{雨|あめ}が{少|すく}なくなりました is the narrator's line about the weather. The shopkeeper talks about people.

questions.prompt: {来週|らいしゅう}、{何|なに}をしますか。

options.why: That was tonight ({夜|よる}), not next week.

options.text: {犬|いぬ}と{町|まち}に{行|い}きます
options.why: That was this afternoon ({午後|ごご}).

readings.title: {九州|きゅうしゅう}の{駅|えき}で

paragraphs.ja: {九州|きゅうしゅう}の{小|ちい}さい{駅|えき}で{電車|でんしゃ}を{下|お}りました。{西口|にしぐち}を{出|で}ると、{前|まえ}に{道|みち}が{一|ひと}つだけありました。
paragraphs.en: I got off the train at a small station in Kyushu. When I went out the west exit, there was just one road in front of me.

paragraphs.ja: {地図|ちず}を{見|み}ましたが、{店|みせ}の{場所|ばしょ}が{分|わ}かりません。タクシーもいません。
paragraphs.en: I looked at the map, but I couldn't work out where the restaurant was. There were no taxis, either.

paragraphs.ja: {駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くにいた{女|おんな}の{人|ひと}に、{住所|じゅうしょ}を{見|み}せました。
paragraphs.en: I showed the address to a woman who was near the station.

paragraphs.ja: 「ああ、この{店|みせ}は{有名|ゆうめい}ですよ。{和食|わしょく}の{店|みせ}です。{歩|ある}いて{十分|じゅっぷん}ぐらいです。」
paragraphs.en: "Oh, that place is famous. It's a Japanese restaurant. About ten minutes on foot."

paragraphs.ja: {私|わたし}は{東|ひがし}に{歩|ある}きました。{道|みち}は{長|なが}かったですが、{空気|くうき}がよかったです。
paragraphs.en: I walked east. The road was long, but the air was lovely.

paragraphs.ja: {店|みせ}の{人|ひと}はとても{元気|げんき}で、{和食|わしょく}は{本当|ほんとう}においしかったです。
paragraphs.en: The staff were really cheerful, and the food was truly delicious.

questions.prompt: どの{出口|でぐち}から{出|で}ましたか。
questions.en: Which exit did you leave by?

options.why: 「{西口|にしぐち}を{出|で}ると」: the west exit.
{東|ひがし} comes later: you walked east ({東|ひがし}に{歩|ある}きました) after leaving by the west exit.
{北口|きたぐち} is the north exit. The passage says {西口|にしぐち}.

questions.prompt: {店|みせ}まで{歩|ある}いてどのぐらいですか。
questions.en: How long a walk is it to the restaurant?

options.why: Here {十分|じゅっぷん} means "ten minutes." You know the same kanji from WaniKani as {十分|じゅうぶん}, "enough"; context decides which one it is.
She says about ten minutes. The road only felt long ({道|みち}は{長|なが}かった).
{十日|とおか} is ten days (or the 10th of the month), not ten minutes.

questions.prompt: どんな{店|みせ}ですか。
questions.en: What kind of place is it?

options.text: {有名|ゆうめい}な{和食|わしょく}の{店|みせ}
options.why: 「{有名|ゆうめい}ですよ。{和食|わしょく}の{店|みせ}です」: a famous Japanese restaurant.
A コンビニ never comes up. She calls it {和食|わしょく}の{店|みせ}.
It's about ten minutes' walk from the station, so it isn't inside it.

questions.prompt: {女|おんな}の{人|ひと}に{何|なに}を{見|み}せましたか。
questions.en: What did you show the woman?

options.why: 「{住所|じゅうしょ}を{見|み}せました」: the address.
You looked at the map yourself ({地図|ちず}を{見|み}ました), but you showed her the address.
Your name never comes up here.

paragraphs.ja: {生|なま}ビール……{五百円|ごひゃくえん}　／　お{茶|ちゃ}……{二百円|にひゃくえん}
paragraphs.en: Draft beer: 500 yen / Tea: 200 yen

paragraphs.ja: {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}と{玉|たま}ねぎ……{千円|せんえん}　／　{豚肉|ぶたにく}……{八百円|はっぴゃくえん}　／　{竹|たけ}の{子|こ}（{小皿|こざら}）……{三百円|さんびゃくえん}
paragraphs.en: Beef and onions: 1,000 yen / Pork: 800 yen / Bamboo shoots (small plate): 300 yen

paragraphs.ja: {店|みせ}の{人|ひと}：「{今日|きょう}は{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}が{人気|にんき}ですよ。」

paragraphs.en: Me: "Then one beef and onions, and two draft beers, please."

paragraphs.en: Staff: "Sure. How about the bamboo shoots too? They're at their best right now."

paragraphs.ja: {私|わたし}：「じゃあ、それも{一|ひと}つお{願|ねが}いします。」
paragraphs.en: Me: "Then one of those too, please."

questions.prompt: {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}と{玉|たま}ねぎはいくらですか。
questions.en: How much is the beef and onions?

options.why: {千|せん} is a thousand: 1,000 yen.
{百|ひゃく} is a hundred. The menu says {千円|せんえん}.
{一万|いちまん} is ten thousand. That would be some beef.

questions.prompt: {生|なま}ビールをいくつ{注文|ちゅうもん}しましたか。
questions.en: How many draft beers did you order?

options.why: 「{生|なま}ビールを{二|ふた}つ{下|くだ}さい」: two.
{一|ひと}つ goes with the beef and onions. The beer is {二|ふた}つ.
Nobody says {三|みっ}つ. The order is {二|ふた}つ.

questions.prompt: {店|みせ}の{人|ひと}は、{何|なに}が{人気|にんき}だと{言|い}いましたか。
questions.en: What did the staff say was popular?

options.why: 「{今日|きょう}は{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}が{人気|にんき}ですよ」
{豚|ぶた} is pig, so {豚肉|ぶたにく} is pork. The popular dish is {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}, beef.
The staff recommends {竹|たけ}の{子|こ} next because it's in season ({今|いま}が{一番|いちばん}おいしい), but the popular dish is {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}.

questions.prompt: {全部|ぜんぶ}でいくらですか。
questions.en: What's the total?

options.text: {二千三百円|にせんさんびゃくえん}
options.why: Beef and onions 1,000 + two beers 500 × 2 + bamboo shoots 300 = 2,300 yen.

options.text: {千八百円|せんはっぴゃくえん}
options.why: That counts only one beer: 1,000 + 500 + 300. You ordered {二|ふた}つ.
That leaves out the {竹|たけ}の{子|こ} (300 yen) you added at the end.
